Studio
About

Oz Dabach

EVOXEL · Producer, Mixing & Mastering Engineer

With over a decade of real, practical and proven experience in electronic music, Oz specializes in production, mixing and mastering.

His productions, mixes, and artists using his sample and preset packs have reached labels like Armada, Spinnin' Records, Make The Girls Dance and Tomorrowland Music, played at stages like Ultra, Coachella, EDC, Tomorrowland, MDLBEAST and Laroc Club, and earned support from artists like Armin van Buuren, Keinemusik, HUGEL, KSHMR, Timmy Trumpet, SIDEPIECE, Lucas & Steve and many more.

Part of his catalog goes out under his own artist project (Evoxel). A larger part goes out under other artists' names.

If you have a track that's almost there, a mix that won't translate, or an idea you want built from the ground up, let's work together.

Aki Cohen

Mixing & Mastering Engineer

Known for powerful, musical mixes and masters, Aki combines technical precision with a carefully selected collection of high-end converters and analog equipment to bring every production to its fullest potential. From delicate classical performances to bass-heavy club records — always preserving emotion, dynamics, and tight low-end. Every project is meticulously refined to translate consistently across all listening environments, from everyday streaming to massive festival stages.

Manley Massive Passive

Manley's hand-built tube passive mastering EQ. The gold standard for broad, musical, three-dimensional tone shaping — the kind of analog depth plugins only imitate.

Black Box HG-2

Black Box Analog Design's tube saturation. Pentode and triode warmth with transformer weight and harmonic density that make a master feel alive and expensive.

Crane Song Avocet IIA

A mastering-grade monitor controller with pristine, reference-class internal conversion. We never compromise on what we hear — every decision in the room is made through this high-end listening chain, because a master is only as good as the monitoring behind it.

RME Fireface UFX III

The studio's digital hub — RME's flagship interface with SteadyClock FS for rock-solid, ultra-low-jitter timing and legendary driver stability. Feeds the Prism digitally.

Prism Sound Orpheus

Mastering-grade AD/DA conversion. Prism's converters are a reference standard in the world's top studios — utterly transparent, precise and uncoloured.

SSL Fusion

SSL's analog master-bus processor — Vintage Drive saturation, Violet EQ air, HF compression and transformer colour to finish and glue the mix.

SSL Bus Compressor

The legendary SSL bus compressor — the 'glue' behind decades of hit records. Cohesion, punch and depth pulled across the whole mix.

Crane Song HEDD 192

Crane Song's reference AD/DA with switchable triode and pentode harmonics, adding analog warmth and dimension on the way back into the box.

Answers
FAQ

Choose the service, set the options, and send the request. You will receive a summary message detailing the work terms and a PayPal payment link. Work starts once payment is confirmed.

  1. Choose the service — ghost production, mixing, or mastering.
  2. Set the options — stem count, extra versions, and anything the service offers. The total updates as you go.
  3. Tell us about the project — genre, references, deadline, and a link to a demo if you have one.
  4. Request booking — you will receive a summary message with the agreed work terms, file delivery instructions, and a PayPal payment link.
  5. Payment confirms the slot — work starts once payment is received, and the first version arrives within the stated delivery time.

With processing on, except anything on the master bus. Your track has to keep the identity and aesthetics you built as a producer; the job here is to polish it, not to redo your sound design.

The exception: processing you are not sure about, like excess reverb, saturation or compression you do not love. Remove it, and mention in the project notes what was removed. The more context, the better the decisions.

Mastering — up to 3 business days. Mixing — up to 7 business days. Music Production — typically 12 to 20 business days. Ghost production — agreed per project, depending on scope.

Times apply to the first version. When the studio is at higher volume than usual, slight delays are possible and you will be told upfront.

Reasonable revision rounds are included, and the track is not done until it is right. One ask: listen on several systems and collect all your notes into one list before sending.

Revisions that change the foundations are quoted separately, for example a new arrangement structure, or replacing kick and bass, which by nature requires a new mix and master. Those are billed separately after a quote.

Payment runs through PayPal. After you request the booking, the summary message includes a secure payment link. Payments are made in advance and confirm the booking.

Got a project with special requests — a specific number of tracks, a specific number of mixes, or anything else outside the ordinary — or a service that isn't listed under "Choose the service"? That gets a custom quote. Get in touch and we'll work out the details with you.
